title: A clip's own sound always sits right under its video, visibly attached
goal: The sound that came with a recording belongs to it: on the timeline it is drawn directly under that recording's video row, joined to it so it reads as one clip with two parts, and it stays there when tracks are added, deleted, reordered or the clip moves to another track. Today it lands on whatever audio track is free at the bottom of the timeline (the user's screenshot: the recording on V3, two empty tracks V2 and V1 below it, and its sound on 'Audio' under those), and it shifts around when tracks are inserted or deleted.
notes:
User's words (2026-10-13): "when i delete tracks, or insert, the audio of a track can move around. Audio that is attached to a track should always appear below it, and have some sort of ui affordance that it is attached." Screenshot: tracks V3 (Recording 2026-10-10 at 19.3x), V2 (empty), V1 (empty), Audio (the recording's sound with a volume line), +.

From code reading (not run): PhotonzCore/DocumentTracks.swift trackLayout (~:280-315): a clip's sound ('speakers') goes to its pinned soundTrackID if that audio track is free, else to the first free audio track or a new linked audio track; audio tracks sit in their own section below the video tracks, so the sound is never under its own video. linkedSoundsByTrack (:364), linkedSoundClipIDs (:367), linkedSoundTrackID (:349); track edits addTrack (:520) and deleteTrack (:557). This is a Final Cut style 'audio under its video' model rather than Premiere's A tracks; the user's word decides it. Coordinate with the volume line work (an-audio-clip-answers-right-click-and-its-volume) which draws on this row.
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults with the user's layout (recording on V3, empty V2 and V1, its sound on Audio): add a track above and below, delete V2, move the clip to V1, reorder tracks; record where the sound row goes each time

An attached (linked, not detached) sound is drawn as a sound row directly under its own clip's video track, as part of that track (a sub-row that moves with it), never separated from it by another track; when several clips with sound share a video track, their sounds share that track's sound sub-row (and stack into a second sub-row only where they overlap)

A clear attachment affordance: the video bar and its sound bar are joined (a shared left edge bracket or connector line between them, the same tint family, a small link mark on the sound bar), and picking either shows both as one clip; the track header shows the sub-row as belonging to its video track (indented under it, no separate A track name)

Adding, deleting or reordering tracks and moving the clip between tracks always keeps the sound directly under its video; MEASURED by a walk that does each of these and checks the sound row's position
Detach Audio turns the sound into its own clip on a real audio track (the Audio section at the bottom), losing the attachment affordance; Attach (or undo) brings it back under the video
Mute and volume work as today on the attached row; the volume line rules from the volume line task apply
Old documents open with attached sounds under their videos; pinned soundTrackID values migrate
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Reproduced first (core scratch test at Next defaults): recording moved to V3 with V2, V1 empty showed V3 | V2 | V1 | Audio(sound), exactly the user's screenshot; carrying the Audio track put the sound above all the video. After the change every step keeps '<track> sound' directly under the clip's track.

Before building: a Premiere editor expects A tracks at the bottom, a Final Cut editor expects audio inside the clip; the user's request (2026-10-13) decides for under-the-video. Risks found and handled: a picture carried down passes over its own sound row (handled: the row counts as its track for a drop), the track header carry left the sound row behind (handled: lifts together), an always-present empty Audio row would have shifted every recording walk by a row (dropped: Audio appears only when nothing makes sound, as before).

After building: walked it on the probe (a-clip-s-sound-stays-under-its-video-walk, 7 real pictures). Found and fixed a stale-row bug: the track carry did not re-measure rows after a previous carry, so a second carry aimed at old positions.

Rough items: tint family of the two bars -> filed a-clip-s-picture-and-sound-bars-wear-one-tint-fa with a decision card. Left rough (below the bar): the header elbow and link mark are small and faint; a single clip dragged down travels two rows to pass its own sound row. Walk dragTrack failures now print the rows the carry read.

A clip's own sound is drawn on a row of its video track, directly under it, with an elbow and link mark in the header and a staple joining the bars; it stays there through adding, deleting and carrying tracks and moving the clip (DocumentTrack.attachedTo, trackLayout). Detach Audio goes to an Audio track at the bottom; Re-attach and Undo bring it back. Old documents migrate. Verified: AttachedSoundRowTests (19) and the full suite green; new walk a-clip-s-sound-stays-under-its-video-walk measures the row after each edit (7 real pictures); 20 walks updated and rerun green, plus all 32 caption walks.
